subject: Proportional surge orchestration & autoscale proposal for Corelytics
messages:
From: Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@corelytics.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Corelytics Procurement <procurement@corelytics.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production sizing follow-up / surge windows

Hi Aditya —

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. A couple of follow-ups from our ops and finance teams:

- Corelytics has two predictable seasonal peaks (Oct and Mar) where inference traffic can spike ~2.5–3x baseline for up to 48 hours. We also expect frequent smaller bursts (~1.6x) during product demos.
- Procurement wants to understand how Redwood will handle short-duration spikes without forcing us to over-commit on reserved capacity.
- We need clarity on eviction behavior for preemptible GPUs and how that impacts SLA and retry/backoff for our users.

Can you put together a proposal for a scaled provisioning approach that includes a short-term guaranteed uplift (for critical periods), an elastic shoulder for demo-level spikes, and an autoscale policy that avoids noisy, frequent evictions? Also please include indicative pricing and any crediting model for unused burst hours.

Erin
Erin Walsh
VP of Platform & Operations, Corelytics

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@corelytics.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jun 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production sizing follow-up / surge windows

Hi Erin —

Appreciate the detail — this is very actionable. Looping in Priyom (capacity planning) and Neha (security/compliance) to shape a concrete plan. High-level thoughts up front:

- Two-tier approach: (1) Small guaranteed reserve (customer-owned dedicated pool) sized to your expected baseline + 20% cushion, and (2) an elastic shoulder that can scale up to 3x baseline using preemptible capacity with controlled eviction windows.
- Autoscale: recommend a proportional scaling policy based on a 5-minute moving average with a soft-start ramp (30% capacity added in first 5 minutes, up to target over 20 minutes) to avoid oscillation.
- Canary: run a 72-hour canary at 60% of expected peak before any larger seasonal event.
- Crediting: propose refund credits for unused guaranteed uplift hours when monthly consumption falls below a threshold (details in the capacity matrix).

Priyom/Neha — can you add concrete numbers and ops playbook? Erin — we should schedule a 30-min call to finalize commitments and a proposed canary window next week.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@corelytics.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jun 2028 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Production sizing follow-up / surge windows

Aditya / Erin —

Drafting a practical autoscale and eviction approach below (ops-first, minimizes risk for Corelytics apps):

1) Baseline sizing and guaranteed reserve
- Baseline tokens/sec profile => reserve = baseline * 1.20 (20% cushion). This is customer-dedicated capacity with SLA.

2) Elastic shoulder (preemptible expansion)
- Shoulder available up to 3x baseline for transient spikes. Shoulder uses a mix of preemptible GPUs (cost-efficient) and opportunistic ephemeral units.
- Eviction behavior: preemptible instances will be drained with a 90-second graceful window; long-running requests will be retried by Redwood runtime with adaptive backoff.

3) Autoscale policy (proportional + smoothing)
- Trigger metric: 5-minute moving average of per-second token backlog and 95th pct latency breach.
- Scale step: proportional to deficit (min 10% incremental, max 50% per 5-minute step).
- Soft-start: when deficit detected, add 30% of target within first 5 minutes, remainder over next 15 minutes if pressure persists.
- Cooldown: 20 minutes after a downscale to avoid flapping.

4) Canary & safety bands
- Canary: 72-hour at 60% of predicted peak; monitor latency, error rates, and queue growth.
- Safety bands: hard cap on shoulder expansion per 24h and daily/weekly budget avoidance to protect other tenants (we can expose per-deal burst budgets).

5) Cost & crediting model (indicative)
- Guaranteed reserve priced at committed monthly CU (compute units) rate.
- Shoulder billed at real-time unit rates; if shoulder capacity remains unused against a reserved uplift for the month, we credit unconsumed uplift at 30% of the committed CU rate.

6) Operational runbook highlights
- Auto-fallback: if preemptible eviction rate > 5% in a 1h window, fall back to lower-latency pinned instances (short-term) and notify CS + customer.
- Alerts: token backlog > 10x baseline for 5m => paged to oncall.

I've attached a capacity matrix that maps example baseline profiles to reserve/shoulder numbers and estimated monthly cost ranges.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@corelytics.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Jun 2028 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Production sizing follow-up / surge windows

Thanks for the plan — a few security/compliance items to call out for Corelytics (since this will be a Dedicated customer with private data flows):

- Private control plane and VPC peering required for the guaranteed reserve (we will not place customer data on mixed-tenancy control planes).
- Preemptible/ephemeral shoulder instances cannot access persistent customer KV caches; KV and prefix cache stores must remain on dedicated hardware or encrypted network volumes with access controls.
- Audit log continuity: evictions and failover events must be immutably logged and made available to Corelytics for a rolling 90-day window (we can include this in the contract appendix).
- SOC 2 / ISO evidence: attach standard evidence pack (we will link SOC 2 summary + data flow diagram).

I'm attaching the capacity-matrix-corelytics.xlsx and a short draft (proportional-autoscale-draft.docx) that captures these compliance guardrails. Priyom — please verify that the proposed canary instrumentation emits the required audit events (eviction start/end, KV point-in-time snapshot).

Neha Kapoor
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@corelytics.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Corelytics Procurement <procurement@corelytics.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production sizing follow-up / surge windows

Erin —

Thanks — below is a concise proposal and next steps so legal/procurement have something concrete:

Proposal summary
- Guaranteed reserve: baseline * 1.20 (dedicated pool, SLA-backed)
- Elastic shoulder: up to 3x baseline using preemptible capacity with 90s graceful drain and adaptive backoff for long requests
- Autoscale: proportional scaling based on 5-min moving average with soft-start ramp (30% first 5m, up to target over 20m); 20m cooldown on downscale
- Canary: 72-hour run at 60% of forecast peak; add instrumentation and audit events per Neha's notes
- Crediting: unused uplift credited monthly at 30% of committed CU rate (detailed in capacity matrix)

Next steps
1) Procurement review & MOU: Redwood to share MOU with the above SOW appendix and crediting table (we'll draft this by EOD Wed).
2) Canary window: propose Jul 9–11 as the canary (we can shift depending on Corelytics availability).
3) Technical kickoff: Priyom will schedule a 60-min runbook walk-through with your ops team.

Attachments: capacity-matrix-corelytics.xlsx, proportional-autoscale-draft.docx
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/CLT-2028-042

If that looks good, I'll route the MOU to procurement and legal.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@corelytics.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Corelytics Procurement <procurement@corelytics.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 18:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production sizing follow-up / surge windows

Aditya / Team —

This plan looks reasonable and aligns with what Procurement needs to move forward. Two small asks before MOU:

1) Contract language for "graceful throttling" — we need a short clause that states Redwood will use best-effort retries and provide a measurable signal to Corelytics when throttling occurs (token backlog and latency metric).
2) Monthly burst usage report — procurement wants a simple CSV export each month that lists uplift hours consumed vs committed and credits applied.

Jul 9–11 works for the canary. Please send the MOU and we will route internally.

Thanks,
Erin
Erin Walsh
VP of Platform & Operations, Corelytics
